proof:
Source: parent step 1 ("spt C = spt μ"), i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–305: spt T = spt μ_T) together with Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768: μ_T = θH^n⌞M). Simon gives no proof of 3.2(3). Instead of the mass identity M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (whose proof with the contract's Euclidean coefficient norm would need a Cauchy–Binet comparison of covectors with unit simple n-vectors, not available in Mathlib) we prove both inclusions directly from the integral representation; the inclusion U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T uses the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations, which is exactly the consequence "T vanishes on W ⇒ μ(W) = 0" of 3.2(3) that the parent uses ("if C vanishes on all forms supported in B, M_B(C) = μ(B) = 0").

Notation. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ = R.orient, H^n = μHE[n], μ = R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ; thus μ(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dH^n for Borel A and ∫ f dμ = ∫_M θ f dH^n. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support), spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) with spt ω ⊆ W ("T vanishes on W"). spt μ (Measure.support) is the set of x such that μ(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N of x.

1. Preliminaries.
 (a) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ A) ≤ μ(A) for every Borel A; and μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (b) For an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P define δ_τ(w_1,…,w_n) := det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j=1..n}. It is the row-determinant of the n vectors L(w_j) ∈ ℝ^n, L(w) := (⟨τ_i, w⟩)_i, hence n-linear and alternating in (w_j); it is continuous (finite dimension), so δ_τ is an n-covector, and δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det(I) = 1 (for n = 0, δ_τ is the constant form 1).
 (c) For orthonormal τ and every n-covector α, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm). Hence if ξ_0 is a unit orientation of an n-plane (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_0 Q: ξ_0(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal spanning Q), then ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1 and ξ_0(δ_τ) = ±1 ≠ 0.
 (d) By R.orients, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an n-plane; since μ ≪ H^n⌞M, (c) gives ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 and ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x.
2. spt T ⊆ U ∩ spt μ. Let x ∈ spt T; then x ∈ U. Suppose x ∉ spt μ, so μ(N) = 0 for some neighbourhood N of x. Since U is open, choose ε > 0 with closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ N ∩ U and put W := ball(x, ε). W is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, ε) is compact and contained in U. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Then ω(y) = 0 for y ∉ W, while H^n(M ∩ W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(N) = 0 by 1(a). Hence y ↦ θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) vanishes H^n-a.e. on M and T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n = 0. So T vanishes on W, i.e. x ∈ W ⊆ Z, contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z. Therefore x ∈ U ∩ spt μ.
3. Claim: if W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U and T vanishes on W, then μ(W) = 0.
 Consider f(y) := ξ(y), a function with values in the Banach space Λ_n = MultiVector P n (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors). f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ is for H^n⌞M, and μ ≪ H^n⌞M) and ‖f‖ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. by 1(d); since μ(W) ≤ μ(closure W) < ∞ by 1(a), f is integrable on W, in particular locally integrable on the open set W. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and spt g ⊆ W, and put I_g := ∫ g f dμ ∈ Λ_n. For every n-covector α the form ω := gα (ω(y) = g(y)·α) is C^∞, compactly supported, spt ω ⊆ spt g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and T(ω) = 0; evaluation at α is a continuous linear functional on Λ_n and commutes with the Bochner integral (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply / integral_comp_comm), so, by the representation and linearity of ξ(y),
 I_g(α) = ∫ g(y) ξ(y)(α) dμ(y) = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(g(y)α) dH^n(y) = R.action(ω) = T(ω) = 0
 (the middle equality is ∫ F dμ = ∫_M θ F dH^n, Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul). Hence I_g = 0 for all such g. By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on an open set, for functions with values in a complete normed space (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, which needs no local finiteness of μ), ξ(y) = f(y) = 0 for μ-a.e. y ∈ W. (Equivalently one may test against the members of a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors; that space embeds linearly and injectively into the finite-dimensional space of n-linear maps, Mathlib Module.Finite for multilinear maps.) By 1(d), ξ(y) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. y. Therefore μ-a.e. point lies outside W, i.e. μ(W) = 0.
4. U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T. Let x ∈ U ∩ spt μ and suppose x ∉ spt T, i.e. x ∈ Z; then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which T vanishes. By step 3, μ(W) = 0; but W is an open neighbourhood of x and x ∈ spt μ, so μ(W) > 0. Contradiction; hence x ∈ U ∖ Z = spt T.
5. Steps 2 and 4 give spt T = U ∩ spt μ, i.e. T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support.
key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on M: a μ-null ball meets M in an H^n-null set, so T vanishes on it; hence spt T ⊆ U ∩ spt μ.
For g ∈ C^∞_c(W): (∫ gξ dμ)(α) = T(gα) = 0 for every covector α, so ∫ gξ dμ = 0 and the (Banach-valued) fundamental lemma gives ξ = 0 μ-a.e. on any W on which T vanishes.
ξ ≠ 0 μ-a.e. (ξ(δ_τ) = ±1 for δ_τ = det(⟨τ_i,·⟩)), so μ(W) = 0 for every piece W of the zero region; hence U ∩ spt μ ⊆ spt T.
